<details class="guide-section"><summary>Overview</summary>

Your first goal is a small documentation contribution. You do not need MRI data or a GPU for this session.

</details>

<details class="guide-section" id="1-get-access"><summary>1 · Get access</summary>

Create a GitHub account. Ask your supervisor for repository access, or agree to use a fork. Read the [contribution workflow](https://github.com/Donggyurim/neuroimaging-training/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before making changes.

**Done when:** you can open the repository and know where your task will be tracked.

</details>

<details class="guide-section" id="2-preview-the-guide"><summary>2 · Preview the guide</summary>

Install [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads) and [Quarto 1.8.27](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/tag/v1.8.27), the version used by this site’s build. If your supervisor has provided a prepared environment, use its existing checkout and Quarto installation.

For a new local checkout:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Donggyurim/neuroimaging-training.git
cd neuroimaging-training
quarto --version
quarto preview
```

Open the address printed by Quarto in your local browser. Stop the preview with Ctrl+C when finished.

**Done when:** the homepage opens and you can navigate to a lesson.

</details>

<details class="guide-section" id="3-make-a-small-useful-change"><summary>3 · Make a change</summary>

[Create a Student task issue](https://github.com/Donggyurim/neuroimaging-training/issues/new?template=student-task.yml) describing one unclear instruction or small documentation improvement. Agree the task with your supervisor. In your repository checkout:

```sh
git switch -c student/first-contribution
```

Edit a relevant `.qmd` page, preview the change, then check the full site:

```sh
quarto render
git status --short
git diff
```

The render should finish with `Output created: _site/index.html`. Review all changed files before committing. Do not add generated `_site/` or `.quarto/` files.

**Done when:** your edit is visible and the full render completes successfully.

</details>

<details class="guide-section" id="4-ask-for-feedback"><summary>4 · Ask for review</summary>

Commit your intended changes, push your branch to the repository you have access to, and open a **draft pull request**. Link the task issue and explain what changed and how you checked it. Ask your supervisor for review, respond to feedback, and follow the repository’s merge process.

**Bring to review:** the task issue, draft PR, and build result. Never push directly to `main`.

</details>

<details class="guide-section" id="when-something-goes-wrong"><summary>Troubleshooting</summary>

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Reference table"}

| What you see | What to try |
|---|---|
| `quarto: command not found` | Reopen your terminal after installation, then check `quarto --version`. In a prepared environment, follow its activation instructions. |
| Preview cannot start on its port | Stop your earlier preview, or run `quarto preview --port 4201`. |
| Render fails | Read the first reported error. Check YAML indentation, file paths, and the page you just edited. |
| Git push is denied | Confirm the remote and your repository access with the supervisor. Use your agreed fork workflow if necessary. |
| You are still stuck | Send the command, error, version, and expected result in your task issue, with sensitive details removed. |

:::


</details>

<details class="guide-section" id="next-plan-your-research"><summary>Next steps</summary>

[Return to your milestones →](../student.qmd)

Agree a small question, a fixed dataset version, access terms, and a compute route with your supervisor. The [structural MRI pathway](structural-mri-pathway.qmd) explains the later stages. Analysis runs separately: a successful website render does not validate an MRI workflow.

</details>
